messages:
maria: quick follow-up from the architecture sync: we need a clear pattern for late credits and how they affect live balances. two candidate flows: lease-first (fast reads) vs event-first (single source of truth). thoughts?

kevin: leaning lease-first for user-visible SLOs. main risk = state retention for long-tail late events.

sylvie: event-first simplifies audits, but queries for current balance will be heavier. we could materialize aggregates in a store for reads.

ritesh: what about a middle-ground: issue short leases for hot reads, always emit immutable events with same canonical id for replay. reconcilers use events to reconcile leases when they expire.

noelle: agree on canonical id. propose naming: `audit_id_v1` and require edge proxy to stamp it at ingress. SDKs should expose header `x-rwd-audit-id`.

maria: good. on TTL, suggest default lease TTL = 8h (captures most retries) with per-tenant override.

kevin: storage: leases in redis cluster for sub-ms lookup. proofs go to a compacted kafka topic (keyed by audit_id) and raw payloads to S3 for long retention.

sylvie: compaction of proofs necessary. we only need the latest proof per audit_id to drive reconciliation, not every duplicate.

ritesh: dedupe logic: consumer should compare `proof_seq` (monotonic) per audit_id and ignore older seqs. define `proof_seq` = ingest_ts + node_counter tie-breaker.

noelle: late-arrival corrections should produce correction events with metadata: audit_id, delta_units, reason_code. billing will either auto-apply or batch depending on size.

infra-bot: rollout note: proofs-producer v0.2 scheduled to canary in 4h.

maria: action items: kevin -> draft TTL/redis sizing (due Tue), sylvie -> minimal proofs schema + compaction rules (due Wed), noelle -> billing correction policy draft (due Wed). If no objections I'll update the RFC with these decisions.

kevin: no objections from infra.

maria: thanks all, closing thread.
